rawAnswer: {"story":{"what":"The change hardens TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo so that types with duplicate keys or mixed int/string keys no longer make the analyzer throw. Members whose key is already taken are no longer added to the intMembers and stringMembers dictionaries a second time. Members whose key kind does not match are skipped once DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys has been reported. The change also adds analyzer tests and execution tests for types with SuppressSourceGeneration = true, a README section on opting out of source generation, and changes the depth check in MessagePackSecurity.DepthStep from >= to >.","why":"Issue 2234 reports that the analyzer stopped working for [MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)] types after 3.1.0. Before this change, a duplicate key reached Dictionary.Add, which throws on a key that is already present, and that exception stopped the analyzer. Now the analyzer reports the diagnostic and keeps going.
